prompt:
PLAN 01 — SESSION BEGINS | TRUST IS GIVEN

Create a 15-second cinematic sequence for Seedance 2.5.
Horizontal 16:9.
Exactly three shots lasting five, four and six seconds.

CHARACTER REFERENCES:
Young Homayoun = {{CHAR_HOMAYOUN_YOUNG}}
Composer = {{CHAR_COMPOSER}}
Father = {{CHAR_FATHER}}

LOCATION REFERENCE:
Early-2000s recording studio, vocal booth and connected control room = {{LOC_RECORDING_STUDIO}}

PROP REFERENCES:
Mixing console = {{PROP_MIXING_CONSOLE}}
Studio microphone and pop filter = {{PROP_MIC}}
Studio headphones = {{PROP_HEADPHONES}}
Lyric sheet = {{PROP_LYRIC_SHEET}}

Preserve the referenced studio architecture, glass partition, console design, microphone, costumes, hairstyles and character appearance.

DRAMATIC STATE:

This is Homayoun’s first important professional recording opportunity.

The emotional tone is concentration, anticipation and the quiet realization that someone has trusted him with a serious recording session.

Homayoun is focused rather than frightened.

The composer represents professional trust.
The father represents personal reassurance.

START STATE AND BLOCKING:

Young Homayoun stands inside the vocal booth facing the microphone.

He wears the studio headphones throughout the sequence and holds the lyric sheet.

The composer sits inside the separate control room behind the mixing console.

The father stands elsewhere inside the same control room, spatially separated from the composer.

A large studio glass partition clearly separates Homayoun from both men.

The composer’s face remains only partially readable throughout the sequence. His identity is communicated through his position behind the console, silhouette, hands and professional actions.

The father remains clearly recognizable.

SHOT 01A | 00:00–00:05 | THE SESSION IS OPENED

Begin inside the control room with a 50mm layered medium-detail shot at seated console height.

Build the frame through multiple depths.

Out-of-focus faders, cables and illuminated meters occupy the near foreground.

The composer sits behind them in the middle distance, partially obscured by the equipment and a soft reflection from the studio glass.

His face remains at a three-quarter or partial angle, never presented as a clean frontal portrait.

The camera makes a slow lateral drift of approximately half a meter across the console.

As the camera passes him, attention naturally transfers from his partially visible figure toward his hand.

His hand raises one fader with deliberate precision, adjusts a single rotary control, then activates the recording function.

Let his professional action establish that the room is ready for Homayoun.

SHOT 01B | 00:05–00:09 | THE YOUNG SINGER

Cut inside the vocal booth to a 40mm medium shot from a slight three-quarter front angle at Homayoun’s eye level.

Homayoun stands at the microphone with the headphones firmly covering both ears.

The lyric sheet rests naturally in his hand.

The control-room glass remains visible behind and beside him so the spatial relationship between the two rooms stays readable.

Homayoun lightly settles the headphones against his ears, straightens his posture and looks through the glass.

His movement is small and deliberate.

His face carries concentration and awareness of the importance of the moment.

Use a quiet handheld drift closer, approximately twenty centimeters.

SHOT 01C | 00:09–00:15 | TWO FORMS OF TRUST

Cut to Homayoun’s visual axis toward the control room, photographed from inside the booth with a 65mm lens.

Use the studio glass as a layered compositional surface.

The composer sits deeper SCREEN-LEFT behind the mixing console.

Foreground equipment, reflections and shallow focus partially obscure his face while keeping his body position and role completely understandable.

He gives Homayoun one small professional cue to begin: a restrained nod accompanied by a minimal hand gesture near the console.

Homayoun’s eyeline then travels slightly across the glass.

The composition gently reframes to reveal his father standing separately deeper SCREEN-RIGHT, with clear empty space between the father and composer.

The father meets Homayoun’s gaze and gives one small, calm nod.

The gesture carries personal assurance rather than rescue.

End on the father’s quiet acknowledgement.

SPATIAL RULE:

Homayoun remains entirely inside the vocal booth.

The composer and father remain entirely inside the control room.

The glass partition is always visually legible between them.

The composer and father occupy separate areas of the control room and never overlap each other or Homayoun in a confusing composition.

The composer is understood through context, silhouette, hand movement and console interaction rather than facial precision.

LIGHT AND IMAGE:

Warm practical studio lighting mixed with soft ambient illumination from the control room.

Use reflections on the studio glass as a natural visual layer.

Allow foreground equipment to drift softly out of focus.

Natural skin texture, restrained early-2000s image character, moderate shallow depth of field and subtle organic camera movement.

SOUND:

Quiet studio room tone.
Soft electrical hum.
Fader movement.
Small console clicks.
Headphone contact.
Controlled breathing.

MUSIC: none.
DIALOGUE: none.

Continue the same warm practical lighting from PLAN 01.

Natural exposure and restrained contrast.

Create a 15-second cinematic sequence for Seedance 2.5.
Horizontal 16:9.
Exactly three shots lasting five, four and six seconds.

CHARACTER REFERENCES:
Young Homayoun = {{CHAR_HOMAYOUN_YOUNG}}
Composer = {{CHAR_COMPOSER}}
Father = {{CHAR_FATHER}}

LOCATION REFERENCE:
Early-2000s recording studio, vocal booth and connected control room = {{LOC_RECORDING_STUDIO}}

PROP REFERENCES:
Mixing console = {{PROP_MIXING_CONSOLE}}
Studio microphone and pop filter = {{PROP_MIC}}
Studio headphones = {{PROP_HEADPHONES}}
Lyric sheet = {{PROP_LYRIC_SHEET}}

Preserve the referenced studio architecture, booth wall treatment, glass partition, console design, microphone, costumes, hairstyles and character appearance.

DRAMATIC STATE:

This is Homayoun’s first serious professional recording opportunity.

The emotional tone is quiet concentration, anticipation and the awareness that this room has made space for his voice.

The composer represents professional trust.
The father represents personal reassurance.

START STATE AND BLOCKING:

Young Homayoun stands inside the vocal booth facing the studio glass and the control room beyond it.

The microphone is positioned between him and the glass, as in a normal recording setup.

He has not yet fully settled into performance.

The studio headphones are present only as the pair that will be placed on his ears. After he places them on, they remain on his head for the rest of both PLAN 01 and PLAN 02. They must never appear hanging elsewhere, resting on furniture, lying on the floor, or detached in any later shot.

The lyric sheet is in his hand.

The composer sits inside the separate control room behind the mixing console.

The father stands elsewhere inside the same control room, spatially separated from the composer.

A large studio glass partition clearly separates Homayoun from both men.

The composer’s face remains only partially readable throughout the sequence. His identity is communicated through his position behind the console, silhouette, hands and professional actions.

The father remains clearly recognizable.

SPATIAL LOCK:
